summary.headline: Capital SFB Q2 FY27: gross advances up 23.4% YoY to INR9,755 crore, PAT up about 31% to INR46 crore, NIM 4.24%.
summary.overview: Gross advances grew 23.4% YoY and 7.5% QoQ to INR9,755 crore, with disbursements of INR1,095 crore (up 36% YoY). Total deposits reached INR10,831 crore (up 16.2% YoY), with CASA at 34.5% and cost of deposits down to 5.68% from 5.92% a year ago. Asset quality improved, with gross NPA at 2.36% and net NPA at 1.12%, while PPOP of INR68 crore and PAT of INR46 crore rose about 31% YoY. Management reiterated the Vision 2029 targets of over INR16,000 crore loan book and 300-plus branches, and flagged a possible regulatory change to bancassurance income.

segments.name: Business loans
segments.commentary: Largest segment at 28% of the book, up from 23% a year ago and 27% last quarter. Management said business loans are growing faster than the overall book.

segments.name: Mortgages (LAP)
segments.commentary: About 24% of advances, down from 26% a year ago and 25% last quarter.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: About 26% of advances, down from 27% last quarter. Agri grew 6.23% QoQ; lending is confined to Punjab and Haryana.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Held deliberately flat at about 14% of advances, lending only to well-rated borrowers.

segments.name: Consumption
segments.commentary: About 7% of portfolio, growing 6.89% QoQ and 21.9% YoY; net NPA 0.47%. Offered mainly as a second or third product to existing customers.

segments.name: Punjab vs outside Punjab
segments.commentary: Outside Punjab has 21% of branches (47), 25.7% of advances and 8.2% of deposits. Outside-Punjab advances grew 39% YoY vs 19% for Punjab; GNPA 0.87% outside vs 2.88% in Punjab.

guidance_outlook: FY27 loan growth guidance was 20-22% at the start of the year; H1 growth was 23%, and management said it is aiming to overachieve.
Vision 2029 targets: gross advances over INR16,000 crore and more than 300 branches by FY29. Management said the current run rate exceeds what is needed.
ROA target of 1.6% by FY29 from 1.39% today, driven by NIM expansion (guided 4.3-4.35%, a 7-12 bps gain) and opex (operating cost to average assets guided 2.80-2.85% by FY29 from about 3.05%).
Target of 30%+ branches outside Punjab by FY29, with out-of-Punjab advances expected at 32-37% of the book.
Universal bank license aspiration after FY29, at a balance sheet of about INR21,000-23,000 crore.
capex_capacity: Network of 222 branches across 5 states and 2 union territories; 77% of branches are in semi-urban and rural centres (SURU), contributing 75% of deposits.
Business per branch outside Punjab reached INR80 crore-plus for branches of 5 years and above, vs INR72 crore at end-Q4 FY26.
Target of more than 300 branches by FY29, with 30%+ outside Punjab.
Rajasthan presence is limited to 7 branches; the bank is following an asset-first approach in new geographies such as Rajasthan and NCR.
Capital adequacy ratio of 20.8% (Tier 1 18.5%), with no immediate need to raise fresh capital.
demand_pricing: Industry credit grew about 19.4% YoY vs deposit growth of about 17.8% as of September 2026.
RBI raised the repo rate by 25 bps to 5.50% in October 2026 and moved to calibrated tightening; management expects rates to stay higher for longer.
Yield on advances was 11% in Q2 FY27, flat YoY and up 10 bps QoQ. The October repo hike has not yet flowed into advance yields.
About 52% of advances are fixed-rate and 48% floating; EBR-linked loans are 13-14% of the portfolio and get a 25 bps EBR increase from 1 November 2026.
Term deposit ATS is about INR12 lakh; savings average ticket is about INR50,000. Retail deposits are over 90% of the total, with rollover above 90%.
Management sees its deposit premium at 25-35 bps over top private sector universal banks.

qa_highlights.question: Is the weak monsoon affecting the agriculture book, and is collection efficiency holding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact is not visible in Punjab and Haryana, citing canal water and tube wells. H1 gross slippage was 1.11% annualised, net slippage 0.24%, and SMA1+2 fell to 3.31%. Early paddy productivity data is the same or better than last year in 25 of 26 districts.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the cost of deposits fallen only 22 bps when the RBI cut rates by 125 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the bank has a premium over peers, a CASA ratio above 34%, and fixed-rate TD repricing. About 60-62% of the benefit has come through repricing, and the cost of deposits is 5.68%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NIM path and the scope to expand it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided NIM to 4.3-4.35% from 4.24%, citing a CD ratio move from 85.4% toward the mid-to-high 80s over 1.5-2 years. It said this can happen without changing deposit or loan pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Why are consumption-loan yields low, and will the bank go to fresh customers via dealers?
qa_highlights.answer: Consumption loans are about 7% of the book, mainly cross-sell to existing customers. About 25-30% is loan against own FDRs at 7.5-8%. Management said pilots are running to fast-track sub-products, but it did not give details.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the draft IRDAI circular on bancassurance, and what is the other fee income plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Bancassurance commission was INR10.2 crore out of INR30 crore non-interest income, about 33%. Management said the bank is waiting for a draft circular, expects an impact that is not material, and cited a 0.92% non-interest income-to-assets ratio. The ROA plan does not rely on fee income.

qa_highlights.question: What are the universal bank aspirations and when will they be pursued?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it aims to apply for a universal bank licence after FY29, at a balance sheet of about INR21,000-23,000 crore, once the bank reaches the FY29 targets.

risks_watch: Weak monsoon and drought in parts of India (management said Punjab and Haryana remain unaffected); watch agri slippages and SMA trends.
Margin pressure if deposit repricing outpaces the loan-yield pass-through in a higher-for-longer rate cycle; yield on advances was flat YoY at 11%.
Bancassurance fee income (about 33% of non-interest income) at risk from the IRDAI draft circular; the bank has not yet detailed alternatives.
Growth and profitability outside Punjab: CASA there is 25.3% vs 35.3% in Punjab, and outside-Punjab deposits are only 8.2% of the total.
CASA ratio fell QoQ (seasonal, per management) in a high term deposit rate environment.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, asset quality and the Vision 2029 targets, with management saying it is growth-hungry and that the run rate exceeds plan. More measured on rates and the IRDAI draft, where it said it is waiting for a draft circular and declined to size the alternatives.
key_quotes: Our priorities are quite simple, remain the same, grow the franchise, strengthen the deposit base and protect the quality of the balance sheet.
We are a growth-hungry organization, and we believe the complete foundation is available to grow.
We will keep lending the way we always have, secured, granular with careful customer selection and strong collection.

adds.what: Branch network expansion toward 300+ branches by FY29 (30%+ outside Punjab); currently 222 branches

growth.why: FY27 advances growth guided at 20-22% (midpoint 21%) and H1 delivered 23% with management aiming to overachieve; backing is partial, rooted in H1 run-rate, a 36% YoY disbursement rise, and the branch and asset-first expansion plan to 300+ branches by FY29, with no specific new-capacity numbers for FY27.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM at 4.24% (vs 4.04% a year ago, 4.21% last quarter) with guidance of 4.3-4.35%, driven by CD ratio moving from 85.4% toward mid-to-high 80s, and cost of deposits down to 5.68% from 5.92%, though yield on advances is flat at 11% with the October repo hike not yet passed through.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Network of 222 branches with a target of 300+ by FY29 (30%+ outside Punjab), and outside-Punjab business per mature branch at INR80 crore-plus; no specific FY27 branch count was given, so the timing is spread out.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Gross advances grew 23.4% YoY to INR9,755 crore and H1 growth was 23% against FY27 guidance of 20-22%, with management aiming to overachieve and disbursements up 36% YoY to INR1,095 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: CAR is 20.8% (Tier 1 18.5%) with no immediate need to raise capital, and the bank is asset-first with no capex or plant plan discussed beyond the branch network.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 advances growth guidance of 20-22% has been exceeded by H1 at 23%, and management said it is aiming to overachieve, though no formal upgrade was announced.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Yield on advances is flat at 11% while cost of deposits is falling only slowly, and the RBI repo hike of 25 bps to 5.50% in October with higher-for-longer rates could squeeze margins; IRDAI draft could hit fee income (bancassurance INR10.2 crore of INR30 crore non-interest income, about 33%).

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management said pilots are running to fast-track consumption sub-products, but it gave no details or timing; consumption loans are about 7% of the book, growing 21.9% YoY.

rows.label: IRDAI draft circular on bancassurance
rows.why: Bancassurance commission was INR10.2 crore out of INR30 crore non-interest income (about 33%); management expects the impact to be not material but has not sized alternatives while awaiting the draft.

rows.label: CD ratio rise to mid-to-high 80s
rows.why: CD ratio is 85.4% and management guided a move toward the mid-to-high 80s over 1.5-2 years, which it says can lift NIM to 4.3-4.35% without changing deposit or loan pricing.

rows.label: Universal bank licence aspiration
rows.why: Application is planned only after FY29 targets are reached, at a balance sheet of about INR21,000-23,000 crore, so it falls outside the 2-4 quarter window.

tone.note: Management was confident on loan growth (23% H1 vs 20-22% guide), asset quality (GNPA 2.36%, SMA1+2 down to 3.31%) and Vision 2029, but measured on rate pass-through and the IRDAI draft, declining to size bancassurance alternatives; analysts pressed on cost of deposits falling only 22 bps against 12
